citation.title: Shangwan Fu et al., A Green Titanium-Cerium Redox Flow Battery with Long-Term Stability via Efficient Capacity Recovery

cell.area_note: 3 cm x 3 cm geometric effective electrode

electrolyte.note: mRFB each tank contains both Ce and Ti, supported by main article page 5 and SI Fig S10; SI p3 line listing mRFB composition repeats sRFB and is inconsistent
electrolyte.source: Main Article pp 5-6 + SI Figs S10-S13

electrochemical.apparent_D_note: Calculated using Randles-Sevcik on porous carbon felt with quasi-reversible CV. Values are unusually high for ordinary molecular diffusivity. Retained as author-reported apparent values with uncertainty; do not treat as independently validated bulk diffusion coefficients.
electrochemical.source: Main Article p5 and SI Table S6 p34

membrane.Hcell_Ti_permeability: not detected in 120 h H-cell (not mathematically zero)
membrane.source: SI Fig S4 p7 and Fig S20 p21

literature_anchor.anchor_note: The long-term run means are NOT the short rate test. 50 and 70 rate values are graph-read approximate, not authoritative numerics.

quantum_chemistry.note: No molecular structure files/basis details or Gaussian license provided; only documentation/review, not DFT replication

source_cautions: SI p3 repeats single-electrolyte wording for the mixed-electrolyte configuration; main article and SI Fig S10 imply both Ti and Ce in both reservoirs.
H-cell membrane geometry not provided; apparent P may not directly transfer to operating cell.
No experimentally measured complete EIS data in SI; only membrane area-specific resistance.
Missing electrode-specific area/flow-field dimensions and raw voltage-time traces; CFD/finite-volume electrochemistry cannot be fully validated.
